card: Configures Nix Windows cross-compilation to default to GCC's POSIX thread model instead of mcf, aligning CI builds with Guix release binaries. Previously, Nix CI used the mcf thread model while official Guix releases used POSIX threads, creating a discrepancy between testing and release binaries (issue #36314). The change supplies winpthreads flags during compiler initialization and logs compiler thread model details in CI.
evidence: Fixes #36314 ('windows: Thread model mismatch between Guix builds and CI').
Author description: 'Guix release binaries use GCC’s POSIX thread model, while the pinned Nixpkgs toolchain defaults to mcf. This makes POSIX the default for Nix Windows cross builds.'
problem: Nix Windows cross-builds in CI defaulted to GCC's mcf thread model, differing from the POSIX thread model used in official Guix release binaries. This created an inconsistency where Windows binaries tested in CI differed in threading behavior and dependencies from production releases.

risk.why: A mistake would only break Nix-based Windows CI tasks or local developer Nix shells.

scope_notes: Small mechanical change to Nix environment definitions and CI initialization scripts (+30/-9 across 2 files).
summary: Configures Nix Windows cross-compilation environments to use GCC's POSIX thread model by default instead of mcf, matching the thread model used in Guix release builds. It also wires in winpthreads headers and libraries to the GCC build and compiler wrapper, while adding a CI step to log the active GCC thread model.
